text.tspan: Page 18, chapter 4 begins: Where do you land?
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
DRAW IT
“visualise this”
Draw the map the opening asks the reader to draw.
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“↳ first we got the reader to draw a graph,
top down; then we [make it evolve?] with a
storyboard, asking the question and the
evolution → the reader will have a Wardley
map”
Build the map in steps: the reader draws a graph top down,
then a storyboard asks the question and adds evolution,
and the reader has a Wardley map. (Two words uncertain.)
DRAW IT
“this needs to be visual”
The models moving right, the way of working on the left:
draw it.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“??? what does this mean [over: gave you the
graph]”
'Everything is connected: graphs gave you the graph' is
unclear.
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“↳ show other types of evolution”
Not only the four stages of activities: show other kinds
of evolution here.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“[struck: A map you cannot be wrong about is
a diagram.]”
Cut.
TOPICS FIRST, DETAILS UNDER THEM
“Don't start with the [where?] [bracket on:
Why do I care so much? In 2022 I gave a talk
Do not open the section with why Dinis cares and his 2022
talk. (The last word is uncertain.)
THE FIRST PAGES SELL THE BOOK
“start here [arrow from: The map also tells
you what to build and what to buy ...]”
Start with what the map does for a founder: what to build,
what to buy, where the market is.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“[struck: Once a thing is on a map, placed
and connected, I stop carrying it in my
head.]”
Cut.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“↳ explain ILC, movements & attention”
Explain ILC (innovate, leverage, commoditise), movement
and attention.
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“[struck: For that talk I made a table of
it.]”
Cut.
